search.decision: No producing source or verbatim copy found in any of the 3 trees for the literal filename 'Finder.Data'. A real Finder APPLICATION source tree does exist at ref/GSOS_6/IIGS.601.SRC/A.U.G/Finder/ (Main.aii, File.aii, etc. -- this is the Finder executable's source, already built elsewhere per project handoff), but it does not contain the string 'Finder.Data' anywhere, and no routine constructing a per-directory desktop-database file by that name was found. system500.hfv (Mac MPW-GM disk) has unrelated Mac-format 'Desktop DB'/'Desktop DF' files (different OS, different format, out of scope). This is consistent with the existing classification: each Finder.Data is a per-directory runtime-computed desktop cache (icon positions/comments for that specific folder's contents) written by the Finder app when it visits that folder -- inherently non-reproducible from any static source file since its content is a function of runtime state, not a build artifact.

Disk 3 of 7 SystemTools1.2mg.notes:
79 files classified. Totals: built 19, buildable-asm 12, buildable-rez 3, pascal-c-nontarget 3, no-source-substitute 41, needs-investigation 1.

BUILT (19, harness-gated byte-exact on the Disk-3 path): Finder (findercheck + finderdatacheck), 5 CDEVs DirectConnect/Keyboard/Modem/Monitor/Sound (cdevcheck), CDRemote NDA (appdatacheck), 5 drivers SCSI.Manager/SCSICD/SCSIScan/SCSITape/RAM5 (drivercheck), 5 FSTs DOS3.3/HFS/HS/Pascal/MSDOS (fstcheck), Tool026/NoteSeq (toolcheck), BASIC.System (basiccheck, which checks the Disk-3 copy explicitly).

BUILDABLE-ASM (12, asm source proven present via GSToolbox/build.tools but NO byte-exact harness yet): 9 drivers (Modem, Parallel.Card, Printer, Epson, ImageWriter, ImageWriter.LQ, StyleWriter, Apple.Midi, Card6850.MIDI — all from GSToolbox/PrinterDrivers or Midi/Drivers) + 3 tools (Tool025/NoteSynth, Tool029/ACE, Tool032/MIDITools). These are the obvious next unlocks — pure assembly, source in-tree, just need harness recipes. Note gsasm already carries a 'Tool025 case-collision' fix, so Tool025 assembly is partly exercised.

BUILDABLE-REZ (3): the Printer/Slots/Time CDEVs. Rez sources exist (A.U.G/CtlPanel/{Printer,Slots,Time}CDEV/*.r) and their Disk-2 twins are byte-exact via cdevcheck, but cdevcheck maps these three names to the DISK2 copies only — the Disk-3 copies are not directly gated. HUMAN DECISION: confirm the D3 copies are byte-identical to the D2 copies (very likely) and add D3 targets to cdevcheck to promote them to built.

PASCAL-C-NONTARGET (3): Calculator (GSCalcNDA.pii, 'Max Pascal'), FindFile (data fork FindFileDA.p is Pascal; its RESOURCE fork IS already byte-exact via rezforkcheck), Adv.Disk.Util (A.U.G/ADU is 11 Pascal .pii files + adu.rii Rez fork). For FindFile and Adv.Disk.Util I picked the classification of the hardest (Pascal code) fork; both have a buildable-rez resource fork.

NO-SOURCE-SUBSTITUTE (41): 32 bitmap fonts + 9 Finder.Data files. Fonts have no producing source in any tree (the only 'font' hits are GSToolbox/QD/font.asm, the QuickDraw renderer, unrelated to the bitmap data; Build.SysTools1 merely Duplicates prebuilt font files). Finder.Data is SUBSTITUTE by rule in diskcheck.py (Finder desktop database).

NEEDS-INVESTIGATION (1): A2.RAMCard (Apple II RAM-card / RamFactor driver). CONFLICT: slinky.aii source exists in GS.OS/Drivers/Slinky, but drivercheck.py explicitly declares '(Slinky not shipped on 6.0.1 disks)' and does not build A2.RAMCard, and no makefile/installer-script maps the name 'A2.RAMCard' to Slinky. Either the drivercheck comment is stale (A2.RAMCard IS Slinky -> buildable-asm) or A2.RAMCard is a different, sourceless driver (-> no-source-substitute). Recommend extracting the golden A2.RAMCard binary and diffing against a Slinky build to resolve.

Fork handling: CDEVs and FindFile/Adv.Disk.Util are dual-fork; where the resource fork is buildable/built but the code/data fork is Pascal or gold-fed, I classified by the hardest (blocking) fork and documented the split in each file's evidence/forks. Every non-Finder.Data path on this disk has a producing source located in ref/GSOS_6/IIGS.601.SRC EXCEPT the 32 bitmap fonts and (pending resolution) A2.RAMCard.

Disk 5 of 7 Fonts.2mg.notes:
Disk 5 (Fonts) is overwhelmingly data. 30 files: 23 outline-bitmap font files (Courier/Helvetica/Times, $C8), 4 Finder.Data desktop DBs, 1 AppleBowl.Icon, plus the Apple.Bowl app and its Read.Me. NOTHING on this disk is currently gated fully byte-exact ('built'=0), but one fork IS proven: Apple.Bowl's RESOURCE fork (863 B, Bowl.r) passes rezforkcheck.py (REZFORK_BYTES_EXACT 4515/4515).

Key findings / human decisions:
1. Apple.Bowl (data+rsrc) = pascal-c-nontarget by its HARDEST part. Its rsrc fork is byte-exact (rezforkcheck), but its DATA fork is the compiled app, produced by 'IntBasicIIGS Bowl.bas' — a custom BASIC->OMF compiler WRITTEN IN PASCAL (A.U.G/Apple.Bowl/Compiler/*.p). That compiler is not the AsmIIGS/Rez target, so the app's code fork is out of scope for byte-exact reproduction unless the project decides to also reproduce IntBasicIIGS. Note BowlBin.aii/ProgAid.aii ARE asm and get linked in, but the bulk (Bowl.obj) is BASIC-compiled.
2. Read.Me (data+rsrc) = buildable-rez and is a low-hanging unlock: Read.Me.r (rStyleBlock resources) builds through the existing gsasm.rez pipeline, and the data fork is a literal copy of Read.Me.txt (Makefile 'Duplicate -d -y'). It's just not wired into rezforkcheck's REZMAP yet — adding it as a 6th target would very likely go byte-exact with no pipeline change.
3. Substitute list (28 no-source): 23 font files, 4 Finder.Data, AppleBowl.Icon. Fonts and icon are authored binary data with no producing source in any of the three trees (verified: find -iname courier*/helvetica*/times.* returned only the QuickDraw Font Manager engine, not the font files). Finder.Data is runtime desktop state (diskcheck hard-codes it SUBSTITUTE by rule).
4. AppleBowl.Icon has an identical archived copy in the source tree, but it is hand-authored data (no Makefile rule builds it) — classified no-source-substitute, not built.

Disk 6 of 7 synthLAB.2mg.notes:
Disk 6 (synthLAB) = 25 files. This is a bundled third-party application disk (Bogas Productions synthLAB) plus its data. In the 6.0.1 build system it is NOT compiled from source — the only tree references are copy scripts (ref/GSOS_6/IIGS.601.SRC/SD.ODDS.N.Ends/APW.Scripts/Build.Synth and .../synthLABToDiskImage) which `Duplicate` prebuilt binaries/data from a source disk (:A2CE_Sources:System Disk 6.0:synthlab:). Hence 23/25 are no-source-substitute.

Two genuine reproducibles:
- MIDI (built): the MIDI CDEV — resource fork byte-exact via work/cdevcheck.py (source MIDICDEV/midi.r), confirmed by running the harness (4552=4552 BYTE-EXACT); data fork empty, so whole file reproduced. Only file on this disk already proven byte-exact.
- Tool035 (buildable-asm): = MIDISynth toolset. Full APW 65816 asm source ships at ref/GSOS_6/IIGS.601.SRC/GSToolbox/MIDISynth/ with a makefile (LinkIIGS ... Tool035) and is listed in GSToolbox/build.tools. This is the obvious next unlock for this disk — toolcheck.py currently gates only up to Tool034, so a Tool035 TOOL_SPEC would extend the tool corpus. NoteSynth (Tool025, already built) and MIDISynth share NoteOn/NoteOff/Update/Tables/Note.Macros filenames — the shared-fork machinery is likely reusable.

Substitute list (verbatim data copies, no source anywhere — need golden bytes shipped): synthLAB app; Icons/SL.Icons; 3x Finder.Data (Icons/, Seq.and.Instr/, root); Reference document (data+rsrc); and 18 sound data files in Seq.and.Instr (*.bnk instrument banks, *.wav waveforms, *.seq sequences).

Human decision: whether the substitute (no-source) files on this disk are in-scope for the byte-exact project at all — synthLAB is a bundled third-party app, distinct from the Apple GS/OS system software. Whole-disk logical-exact for Disk 6 is achievable only by shipping golden bytes for the 23 substitutes plus building Tool035; no diskcheck currently gates Disk 6 (disk_logical_exact to date covers Disk 2 / System Disk).

FORMAT FINDING: The 2mg is a valid 2IMG (magic '2IMG', creator 'XGS!', header len 0x40, image-format field @0x0C = 1 = ProDOS/logical block order, num_blocks @0x14 = 0x0640 = 1600 blocks = 800K, data offset 0x40, data length 0xC8000 = 819200; file size 819264 = 64+819200 checks out).
